record.paper_title: Open problems in renewal, coupling and Palm theory
record.original_question: Let S_n = S_0 + X_1 + ··· + X_n be a renewal process with nonnegative delay S_0 and i.i.d. strictly positive recurrence times X_1, X_2, … independent of S_0. For t ≥ 0 let N_t = inf{n ≥ 0 : S_n > t}, let A_t = t - S_{N_t-1} be the age at time t, let B_t = S_{N_t} - t be the residual life, let D_t = X_{N_t} = A_t + B_t be the total life, and let U_t = A_t / D_t be the relative age. Assume the renewal process is null recurrent, meaning E[X_1] = ∞. Does U_t converge in distribution to a Uniform[0,1] random variable as t → ∞?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.1 Suppose the renewal process is null recurrent. Does Ut still tend in distribution to U as t → ∞?
At = t − SNt−1 = age at time t, Bt = SNt − t = residual life at time t, Dt = XNt = At + Bt = total life at time t, Ut = At /Dt = relative age at time t.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S_0 \ge 0$ be a nonnegative random variable, and let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be i.i.d. strictly positive random variables, independent of $S_0$. Define the renewal process $S_n = S_0 + X_1 + \cdots + X_n$ for $n \ge 0$. For each $t \ge 0$, let
\[ N_t = \inf\{n \ge 0 : S_n > t\}, \qquad A_t = t - S_{N_t - 1}, \qquad B_t = S_{N_t} - t, \]
\[ D_t = X_{N_t} = A_t + B_t, \qquad U_t = A_t / D_t, \]
called respectively the age, residual life, total life and relative age at time $t$. Assume the renewal process is null recurrent in the sense that $\mathbb{E}[X_1] = \infty$.

Question: Does $U_t$ converge in distribution to a Uniform$[0,1]$ random variable as $t \to \infty$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been resolved negatively in general. Work on the ratio of current age to total life for null recurrent renewal processes shows that when the inter-arrival distribution is regularly varying with index $\alpha \in (0,1)$, $A_t/D_t$ converges in distribution to a nondegenerate limit (a generalized arcsine / Beta-type law, e.g. $U^{1/\alpha}$ with $U$ Uniform$[0,1]$ in one parameterization) rather than to Uniform$[0,1]$. Hence the Uniform$[0,1]$ limit characteristic of the positive-recurrent case does not extend to the null-recurrent case.

status_evidence.title: On the Limiting Ratio of Current Age to Total Life for Null Recurrent Renewal Processes
status_evidence.snippet: For renewal processes with inter-arrival distribution regularly varying with index α ∈ (0,1), A(t)/C(t) converges in distribution to a nondegenerate limit expressible via a Uniform[0,1] variable, not Uniform itself.
status_evidence.claim: The limiting distribution of relative age in the null recurrent regularly varying case is not Uniform[0,1], resolving Thorisson's question negatively in general.

status_evidence.title: On the ratio of current age to total life for null recurrent renewal processes
status_evidence.snippet: Further results on the limiting ratio of current age to total life in the null recurrent setting.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent published work confirms the non-uniform limit for relative age in null-recurrent renewal processes.
